name: Le Confort Moderne
funding: Ministère de la Culture (DRAC Nouvelle-Aquitaine), Ville de Poitiers, Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine; non-profit association.

name: Le Cube – independent art room
funding: Small artist-run space founded 2005 by Elisabeth Piskernik; residencies paid by artists, partners are foreign cultural institutes and embassies.
watch: Independent exhibition and residency space at 2 rue Benzerte, with a Vienna branch; still programming in 2026.
records_note: Le Cube names partners only for single exhibitions and publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Le Fresnoy - Studio national des arts contemporains
funding: €5.2M. Ministère de la Culture, Région Hauts-de-France, Métropole Européenne de Lille.

name: Les Ateliers Sahm
funding: Small art centre founded 2012 by Bill Kouélany, funded project by project: Fondation Almayuda (since 2018), Institut français, EU/OACPS (Popul'Art 2023).
watch: Almayuda is a Geneva foundation registered in 2023.
records_note: No site of its own found, only Facebook; no reports, accounts, funder list or board; funder Almayuda names it on its own site.

name: Livingstone Office for Contemporary Arts (LoCA)
funding: Artist-founded non-profit (2014); Perennial partners include Zeitz MOCAA and the National Arts Council Zambia.
watch: Launched the Mosi-oa-Tunya Perennial in Sept 2026; funder roster not public.
records_note: Its Our Sponsors page names 15 partners, undated; a team page lists 13 people, but there is no board, report or accounts.

name: Lothringer 13 Halle
watch: Former machine factory in Haidhausen. Non-profit municipal venue with rotating independent curatorial teams and free admission.

name: Ludwig Museum Budapest
funding: Hungarian state, with the Ludwig Foundation collection.
records_note: The museum posts narrative reports for 2005 to 2025 and budget accounts for 2011 to 2025, shows two undated logos, and names no board.

name: Luma Arles
funding: Funded by the LUMA Foundation of Maja Hoffmann, a Roche heir. Artnet put the total project cost at about EUR 150M.
records_note: States that it was created and funded by the LUMA Foundation of Maja Hoffmann, and publishes no reports, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Lunds Konsthall
funding: Municipal kunsthalle run by Lund municipality.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Lund municipality posts annual reports 2024 and 2025 and lists its culture committee; no funder list.

name: M+ Museum
funding: HKD 380M operating budget, 2.5M annual visitors. West Kowloon Cultural District Authority (statutory body of the Hong Kong SAR Government).
watch: Museum of visual culture in West Kowloon, designed by Herzog and de Meuron.

name: MAC Lima
funding: Private museum in Barranco; sponsors include Fundación Telefónica, Fundación BBVA, Credicorp, UTEC, EU delegation, Getty Foundation, Bloomberg.
watch: Bloomberg is listed as a sponsor. It is under active campaign elsewhere; the atlas lists Bloomberg-roster institutions as B. No protest found at MAC Lima.
records_note: Its Auspicios page shows ten sponsor logos with no date; the site posts no annual reports, accounts or board, and no Peruvian register was found.

name: MAC Montréal
funding: Quebec crown corporation (C$12.5M Quebec grants, 2024-25). Donors: Banque Nationale (lead), Bronfman foundation, Power Corporation, AtkinsRéalis, BMO, RBC, Scotiabank, Desjardins.
watch: AtkinsRéalis (ex SNC-Lavalin) paid C$280M after its Libya fraud guilty plea in 2019. Loto-Québec, named earlier, is not in the 2024-25 report.
records_note: Publishes annual reports back to 2004-05; the 2024-25 report carries audited statements, thanks donors by name and lists the board as of 31 March 2025.
